entry.title: thundersnap 0.01: an undo button for everything
entry.summary: Happy July 4th! For those of us around the world contemplating independence, it's a good day to think about how we came to rely on expensive cloud infrastructure for our fundamental computing needs. With that in mind, here is my latest toy project: an open source tool that makes replicating, forking, sharing, and running container snapshots fast and easy across cloud and personal devices. It's fun to play with, especially on bare metal hardware you run at home, or rent from a provider like Hetzner or OVH. Or, because it uses Tailscale, why not all of them in a single mesh? There's a lot more to say but I don't have time right now. Details are in the README. I will say this: humans and AI agents both want the same things when they're trying to get work done. Ephemeral containers aren't really it. But how about unlimited disk space, fast CPUs, an undo button, and the ability to move to whatever provider offers the best hardware at the best price? That's more like it. Go visit thundersnap on github and tell me what you think!

entry.title: IndieWebClub Bangalore: Special Edition Meetup, A Retrospective
entry.summary: The day after IndieWebClub Bangalore Special Anniversary Meetup, Ankur, Tanvi and I got together and did a retrospective on the event. We noted down what went well, what didn’t, and what we should do the next time. This note summarizes our discussion. What Went Well# We front-loaded many decisions, such as talk format, venue, date, topics etc., and didn’t second-guess them. This helped us later with our tight schedule. We were serious about the CFP from the get-go. We wrote a detailed CFP statement and made a web page for it. This made participants also take it seriously. Life# I took the whole last week off to recover from illness and fatigue. I’m happy to report that all three of us are doing much better now. I worked on them for two days out of seven, which I consider pretty good knowing myself. I spent the rest of the time reading and watching TV, going for walks, and generally resting.
